title: Шинковка и забывчивость  (Knife Skills and Forgetfulness)

segments.t: As German starts the evaluation with vegetable chopping at Claude Monet, Viktor puts on a theatrical display of forgetfulness at Arcobaleno until Elena feels guilty and lets him go. Listen to the Russian scene first.
У вас что-то горит, Виктор Петрович.
Глупая была идея, прости. Я тебя отпускаю.
Ты езжай, за меня не беспокойся. Я тут отдохну немножко.
Let's break this conversation down line by line.
'Viktor Petrovich, hand me a lemon, please.' Elena keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'Here you go.' In spoken Russian, Chef Viktor omits unnecessary linking verbs so the key idea lands immediately.
'I asked for a lemon.' Elena uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
'Let's start with vegetable chopping.' German keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.

'Something of yours is burning, Viktor Petrovich.' Elena keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'Viktor Petrovich, maybe you need some pills?' Elena uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
'Alas, there are no pills for old age.' Chef Viktor uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
'This is my fault.' Elena uses the first-person pronoun in the case required by the Russian verb or preposition.

'It was a foolish idea, forgive me. I am letting you go.' The past-tense verb ending marks the grammatical gender and number of the subject directly.
'Thank you.' Chef Viktor keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'I need to go to the market.' Elena uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.

'You go ahead, don't worry about me. I will rest here a little.' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular pronoun, showing a close or familiar relationship. Now listen to the full Russian exchange again with everything in place.
